In the [[mathematics|mathematical]] study of [[several complex variables]], the '''Szegő kernel''' is an [[integral kernel]] that gives rise to a [[reproducing kernel]] on a natural [[Hilbert space]] of [[holomorphic function]]s.  It is named for its discoverer, the Hungarian mathematician [[Gábor Szegő]].

Let &Omega; be a bounded domain in '''C'''<sup>''n''</sup> with ''C''<sup>2</sup> boundary, and let ''A''(&Omega;) denote the space of all holomorphic functions in &Omega; that are continuous on <math>\overline{\Omega}</math>. Define the [[Hardy space]] ''H''<sup>2</sup>(∂&Omega;) to be the closure in ''L''<sup>2</sup>(∂&Omega;) of the restrictions of elements of ''A''(&Omega;) to the boundary.  The [[Poisson integral]] implies that each element ''&fnof;'' of ''H''<sup>2</sup>(∂&Omega;) extends to a holomorphic function ''P&fnof;'' in &Omega;.  Furthermore, for each ''z''&nbsp;&isin;&nbsp;&Omega;, the map
:<math>f\mapsto Pf(z)</math>
defines a [[continuous linear functional]] on ''H''<sup>2</sup>(∂&Omega;).  By the [[Riesz representation theorem]], this linear functional is represented by a kernel ''k''<sub>''z''</sub>, which is to say
:<math>Pf(z) = \int_{\partial\Omega} f(\zeta)\overline{k_z(\zeta)}\,d\sigma(\zeta).</math>

The Szegő kernel is defined by
:<math>S(z,\zeta) = \overline{k_z(\zeta)},\quad z\in\Omega,\zeta\in\partial\Omega.</math>
Like its close cousin, the [[Bergman kernel]], the Szegő kernel is holomorphic in ''z''.  In fact, if ''&phi;''<sub>''i''</sub> is an [[orthonormal basis]] of ''H''<sup>2</sup>(∂&Omega;) consisting entirely of the restrictions of functions in ''A''(&Omega;), then a [[Riesz–Fischer theorem]] argument shows that
:<math>S(z,\zeta) = \sum_{i=1}^\infty \phi_i(z)\overline{\phi_i(\zeta)}.</math>
